question: Is the Aurzen TravelPlay a good back seat screen for a Tesla Model Y? Where can I buy one?
query: Aurzen TravelPlay review Tesla Model Y compatibility buy 2026

replays.text:
**It could be a good fit if you want a projector screen for parked-car movie nights**, but it isn’t a standalone video display: you’ll need a compatible portable projector. TravelPlay clips in without tools, folds into a carry bag, and doubles as a sunshade. Aurzen lists rear-seat, tailgate, and roof viewing modes, with screen areas of about 47 and 50 inches. [Product details and compatibility](https://aurzen.com/collections/new-releases/products/aurzen-travelplay-autocinema-screen-for-tesla-model-y)

**Check your Model Y’s year before buying:** it’s designed for the 2025–2026 Model Y Refresh. Aurzen says it can fit 2020–2024 models for roof viewing, but the rear screen won’t fully cover the window. Projection is for use only while the car is stationary.

You can [buy it from Aurzen’s U.S. store](https://aurzen.com/collections/new-releases/products/aurzen-travelplay-autocinema-screen-for-tesla-model-y), listed at **$119.99**. Aurzen says it’s available in the U.S. only and includes a 30-day money-back guarantee and one-year warranty.

**It could be a good option for parked-car movie nights**, especially if you have a **2025–2026 Model Y refresh**. TravelPlay is a foldable, clip-in projector screen that also works as a sunshade, with rear-seat, tailgate, and panoramic-roof viewing setups. It includes front and rear panels and a carry bag.

A couple of caveats: **it’s a screen, not a display or projector**—you’ll need a compatible portable projector. It’s intended for use **only while parked**, not while driving. On **2020–2024 Model Ys**, Aurzen says the roof-view setup may fit, but the rear panel won’t fully cover the window.

You can buy it from [Aurzen’s official U.S. store](https://aurzen.com/collections/new-releases/products/aurzen-travelplay-autocinema-screen-for-tesla-model-y), listed at **$119.99**. The listing says it’s available in the U.S. only.
